wire.rules.added.role: one-line receipt after /rules add, painted in the transcript as a notice
wire.rules.added.tone: terse confirmation that names the record
wire.rules.added.note: Placeholders: {id} is the rule's stable id (r1, r2, ...) and {text} is the rule text exactly as stored. {text} is operator-authored and may be any script; keep the receipt on one line around it, and do not rephrase or quote it. The text is repeated here on purpose: the receipt is the only place the accepted wording is shown back, and the record has no undo.

wire.rules.command.role: command description line in /help and the command picker
wire.rules.command.note: The /rules command lists, adds, edits and removes per-session standing rules. No ICU arguments. Width budget: the /help description column is W-26 cells (54 at an 80-column terminal), so a longer sentence truncates in /help and wraps the neighbouring rows.

wire.rules.disabled.role: refusal when /rules runs with the LOP_SESSION_RULES flag off
wire.rules.disabled.tone: plain statement of a switched-off feature
wire.rules.disabled.note: Names the environment variable literally: LOP_SESSION_RULES=1. Keep the variable and its value verbatim; it is the only remedy the sentence offers. No ICU arguments.

wire.rules.empty.role: answer to a bare /rules when the session has no rules
wire.rules.empty.note: Contains the command spelling /rules add <text> verbatim — a technical command, never translated or reordered. The sentence after it is ordinary prose.

wire.rules.line.role: one row of the rule listing printed by a bare /rules
wire.rules.line.note: Placeholders: {id} is a stable technical id (r1, r2, ...) and {text} is the operator's own rule text. Translate only the separator arrangement; keep the id and text verbatim and in that order where the locale's reading direction allows.

wire.rules.no_session.role: refusal when the flag is on but the session has no directory to read
wire.rules.no_session.note: Describes a session-lifecycle state (a session that never materialised a directory), not a user mistake. No ICU arguments.

wire.rules.refused.role: refusal for a rejected /rules add, edit, rm or a bad record
wire.rules.refused.note: Placeholder {reason} is an untranslated technical detail produced by the rules record (for example 'rule text must be a single line' or 'no rule with id r9'). Keep the colon-then-detail shape and never re-capitalise or paraphrase {reason}.

wire.rules.removed.note: Placeholders: {id} and {text}. The text is repeated because removal has no undo — this receipt is the last place the removed rule is shown. Do not rephrase {text}.

wire.rules.unreadable.role: answer to a bare /rules when rules.json exists but is unusable
wire.rules.unreadable.note: Placeholder {reason} is an untranslated validator detail. The sentence states the consequence (no rules are in force) rather than only the failure; keep that clause.

wire.rules.updated.tone: terse confirmation naming the new wording
wire.rules.updated.note: Placeholders: {id} and {text} (the new text). The previous wording is gone; do not keep it in the sentence.

wire.rules.usage.role: usage line for an unknown /rules subcommand
wire.rules.usage.note: Every /rules spelling in this sentence is a technical command and stays verbatim: /rules, /rules add <text>, /rules edit <id> <text>, /rules rm <id>. Only the connective prose ('Use ... or ...') is translated, and the command tokens must not be reordered against each other.
